# 2. Terminology and Conventions

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY, and OPTIONAL in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

The following terms are used throughout:

| **Term** | **Definition** |
| --- | --- |
| Participant | Any entity that transmits or consumes O-CPS messages. Includes vehicles, roadside units (RSUs), and mobile clients (e.g., phones acting as vulnerable-road-user beacons). |
| Vehicle | A participant with longitudinal and/or lateral control authority. |
| RSU | Roadside Unit. A fixed participant, typically maintained by a road authority, that transmits infrastructure messages (SPaT, MAP, environmental) and may relay or fuse nearby vehicle messages. |
| VRU | Vulnerable Road User. A non-vehicle participant (pedestrian, cyclist) that may transmit presence and may consume relevant messages, but has no control authority. |
| Perception Object | A single entity detected by a participant’s sensor fusion: class, pose, kinematic state, confidence, and provenance. |
| World Model | A participant’s current estimate of the set of Perception Objects in its area of interest, fused from its own sensors and received O-CPS messages. |
| Pseudonym Certificate | A short-lived identity certificate issued by an SCMS or equivalent CA, used to authenticate messages without linking them to a persistent vehicle identity. |
| C-ACC Group | A set of two or more vehicles operating under the Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control Group Protocol (§13.1). |
| Leader | The vehicle in a C-ACC Group whose trajectory is used as the coordination anchor. |
| Attestation | A signed claim about the integrity of a participant’s software and sensor stack, used by peers to calibrate trust in that participant’s messages. |
